procedures.title: Japan: Police #9110, Prefectural Cybercrime Consultation Windows (都道府県警察サイバー犯罪相談窓口) and JAFIC

desks.name: Police Consultation Hotline #9110 (警察相談専用電話)
desks.role: National police consultation hotline for general and cybercrime consultation; directs callers to the right prefectural police
desks.how_to_report: Dial #9110 from a mobile phone (or the local prefectural police number listed on the NPA site) and describe the crypto/investment scam; you will be routed to the appropriate prefectural police consulting desk.

desks.name: Prefectural Police Cybercrime Consultation Windows (サイバー犯罪相談窓口) — nationwide list
desks.role: Each prefectural police operates a cybercrime consulting window for online fraud, unauthorized withdrawals, and crypto scams
desks.how_to_report: Use the NPA nationwide directory to find your prefecture's cybercrime consulting window, then phone or visit; for online submission use the NPA unified online intake (via e-Gov, linked from https://www.npa.go.jp/bureau/cyber/soudan.html) which routes your report to the selected prefectural police headquarters or station.

desks.name: Cybercrime Center (サイバー犯罪センター) / JAFIC
desks.role: National Police Agency joint financial-crime intelligence center; coordinates fraud asset tracing (JAFIC = Japanese Alert Network for Financial Crime / 犯罪収益移転防止対策支援センター)
desks.how_to_report: Prefectural police submit coordinated fraud reports here; victims should report through local police, who can invoke JAFIC asset-tracing for crypto scams (commonly used for virtual-currency freezing requests under the 振り込め詐欺救済法 regime).

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank/exchange immediately by phone to request a freeze/recovery of the transfer (振り込め詐欺救済法 procedures within minutes of sending). For crypto, contact the exchange and request withdrawal freeze; ask the bank to contact the receiving bank.
Gather evidence: Keep emails, LINE/chat logs, wallet addresses, transaction hashes (txid), bank transfer statements, and the scammer's contact info; take screenshots.
Report to exchange: Notify the crypto exchange or bank account involved so they can freeze and trace the funds.
Report to police: Call #9110 or your prefectural cybercrime consultation window; submit 被害届 (criminal complaint) at the local station.

Regulator/other: For suspected unlicensed investment advice, report to the Financial Services Agency (金融庁) via https://www.fsa.go.jp/soudan/index.html; consumer hotline #188 (消費者ホットライン) at https://www.consumer.go.jp/hotline.

procedures.title: Japan: Anti-Phishing Council, Investment Advisory Association (JSAIPA/JIAA), FSA consumer desk, Consumer Hotline #188

desks.name: Phishing Countermeasures Council (フィッシング対策協議会)
desks.role: Industry/industry-government council that receives phishing-site and phishing-scam reports and publishes real-time alerts
desks.how_to_report: Submit the phishing URL from their website report form; they distribute takedown requests and warnings.

desks.name: Japan Investment Advisers Association (日本投資顧問業協会 / JSAIPA-related consultation desk)
desks.role: Industry association that answers questions about licensed investment advisers and impersonation/investment fraud
desks.how_to_report: Use the 'お問い合わせ/相談' (contact/consultation) desk on the association homepage; also consult their impersonation and investment-fraud guidance pages under /contact/.

desks.name: Financial Services Agency (金融庁) — consulting windows
desks.role: Financial regulator; publishes counseling windows for debt, investment, and fraud; issues warnings on crypto/investment scams (e.g. 2022 warning on crypto investment fraud: https://www.fsa.go.jp/news/r4/sonota/20221004.html)
desks.how_to_report: Phone the Financial Services Hotline (0570-016811) or submit via the FSA consultation pages; for suspected unlicensed crypto business, report directly to FSA or the prefectural public safety commission (crypto exchange licensing under FIEA/PSEA is enforced with police).

desks.name: Consumer Hotline #188 (消費者ホットライン)
desks.role: National consumer hotline run by Consumer Affairs Agency + local consumer centers; first-line triage for investment/trading scams
desks.how_to_report: Dial 188; you will be transferred to the local consumer affairs center for consultation and, if needed, filing.

desks.name: National Consumer Affairs Center (国民生活センター) — consultation map
desks.role: Receives consumer complaints nationwide; issues alerts on crypto/investment scams
desks.how_to_report: Use the center map to find your local consumer center; in-person or phone consultation available.

steps: Freeze: Same-day bank/exchange freeze via phone (振込詐欺救済法); for crypto, notify the exchange's customer fraud desk immediately.
Gather evidence: Save contract documents, chat logs, wallet addresses, txids, bank statements, and the website/screenshot of the fake platform.
Report to exchange/operator: Report the receiving wallet to the exchange (they may have frozen similar addresses) and your bank.
Report to police: #9110 or prefectural cybercrime window (see the Japan police entry).

Regulator: Report unlicensed advice to FSA (https://www.fsa.go.jp/soudan/index.html) and phishing to the Phishing Countermeasures Council (https://www.antiphishing.jp/); consumer triage via #188 (https://www.consumer.go.jp/hotline).

procedures.title: United States: FBI IC3, FTC, SEC, CFTC, State Attorneys General

desks.name: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
desks.role: Primary federal intake for internet-based crime including cryptocurrency fraud and investment scams
desks.how_to_report: File at https://complaint.ic3.gov/ with details of the scam, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and dollar losses; recovery-fraud scams (people claiming they can recover crypto) should also be reported here (see https://www.ic3.gov/PSA).

desks.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) — ReportFraud.ftc.gov
desks.role: Consumer complaint intake feeding FTC enforcement and Consumer Sentinel (data shared with law enforcement worldwide)
desks.how_to_report: Submit the report online at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/ or via https://consumer.ftc.gov/; include scam communications and payment/crypto details.

desks.name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) — Tip, Complaint, Referral (TCR)
desks.role: Regulator of securities; handles fraudulent crypto investment/token offerings and broker fraud
desks.how_to_report: Submit at https://www.sec.gov/tcr (reported through the 'Report Suspected Securities Fraud or Wrongdoing' page, https://www.sec.gov/submit-tip-or-complaint/tips-complaints-resources/report-suspected-securities-fraud-or-wrongdoing); include the offering documents, platform names, and communications.

desks.name: Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
desks.role: Regulator of futures/commodities and digital-asset derivatives; takes tips and complaints on fraudulent crypto trading platforms
desks.how_to_report: File a tip or complaint at https://www.cftc.gov/complaint or via the CFTC whistleblower program at https://whistleblower.gov/; check the CFTC RED list before investing: https://www.cftc.gov/LearnAndProtect/Resources/Check/redlist.htm

desks.name: State Attorneys General
desks.role: State-level consumer-protection and securities enforcement; each state AG office accepts consumer fraud complaints
desks.how_to_report: Find your state AG via https://www.usa.gov/stop-scams-frauds and file a consumer-fraud complaint; many states also have dedicated investor-protection bureaus.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank/credit union to stop or reverse wire transfers; notify your crypto exchange to freeze the withdrawal; place fraud alerts with credit bureaus.
Gather evidence: Keep all emails/texts, screenshots, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, bank transfer confirmations, and the scam website URL.
Report to exchange/platform: Notify the exchange's fraud/compliance desk so they can freeze or trace the funds; request an internal investigation.
Report to police/federal: File at IC3 (https://complaint.ic3.gov/), and optionally your local police department for a police report number.

Regulator: File with SEC (https://www.sec.gov/tcr) for token/securities fraud, CFTC (https://www.cftc.gov/complaint) for derivatives/futures fraud, FTC (https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/) for consumer fraud, and your state AG (https://www.usa.gov/stop-scams-frauds).

procedures.title: United Kingdom: Action Fraud / Report Fraud and FCA consumer reporting

desks.name: Action Fraud (now branded 'Report Fraud', run by City of London Police)
desks.role: UK's national fraud and cybercrime reporting centre; the primary police intake for crypto/investment fraud
desks.how_to_report: File online at https://www.reportfraud.police.uk/ (legacy URL https://www.actionfraud.police.uk/ redirects here) or call 0300 123 2040; receive a crime reference number for bank/exchange follow-up.

desks.name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
desks.role: UK financial regulator; accepts reports of suspected scam investment platforms (including crypto) and maintains warning lists
desks.how_to_report: Use https://www.fca.org.uk/consumers/report-scam or the FCA contact page https://www.fca.org.uk/contact; check the FCA Warning List before investing.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank's fraud team immediately (UK banks are signatories of the Contingent Reimbursement Model); for crypto, ask the exchange to freeze the withdrawal and to cooperate with police tracing.
Gather evidence: Save chats/emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, bank transfer details, and the scam website URL; take screenshots.
Report to exchange: Notify the crypto exchange or bank involved; request trace/freeze support.
Report to police: File at Action Fraud (https://www.reportfraud.police.uk/) or call 0300 123 2040; for Scotland call Police Scotland 101.
Regulator: Report to FCA (https://www.fca.org.uk/consumers/report-scam); check FCA warning list first.

procedures.title: Germany: BaFin consumer complaint desk and state police (Online-Wache)

desks.name: BaFin (Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht) — Consumer complaints & financial fraud
desks.role: Federal financial regulator; maintains consumer-fraud pages on investment scams (Anlagebetrug), issues unauthorized-entity warnings, handles complaints about regulated entities and unauthorized crypto custodians
desks.how_to_report: Use the BaFin consumer complaint & dispute-resolution page above, or the financial fraud guidance page https://www.bafin.de/DE/verbraucherinnen-verbraucher/themen-finanzprodukte/finanzbetrug-erkennen/finanzbetrug-erkennen_node.html; report suspected unauthorized crypto/business activity via BaFin contact desk.

desks.name: Polizei (state police) — Online-Wache / local police stations
desks.role: Criminal complaint intake (Strafanzeige) for investment fraud, phishing, and crypto scams; each state (Land) police operates an Online-Wache for online filing
desks.how_to_report: File a Strafanzeige online via your state police's Online-Wache (find your state police via https://www.polizei.de/ national portal; e.g., Berlin: https://www.berlin.de/polizei/) or in person at any police station.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank immediately for a transfer recall (Überweisungsrückruf); for crypto, notify the exchange's compliance desk to freeze withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Preserve chats, emails, wallet addresses, txids, bank transfer receipts, and the scam website; German police will ask for these.
Report to exchange/platform: Notify the receiving exchange or bank; German banks can use the CyberAlliance against fraud (CyberAllianz) channels.
Report to police: File a Strafanzeige at your local station or Online-Wache (state police portals via https://www.polizei.de/).

Regulator: Report to BaFin (https://www.bafin.de/DE/verbraucherinnen-verbraucher/hilfe-kontakt/beschwerden-streitschlichtung/beschwerden-streitschlichtung_node.html); check BaFin's unauthorized business warnings.

procedures.title: France: Pharos online signalement, Tracfin financial-intelligence reporting, AMF Épargnants desk

desks.name: Pharos (Plateforme d'harmonisation, de recensement et d'analyse des signalements)
desks.role: National police (Ministry of Interior) online reporting platform for cyber-malveillance, scams, and fraud
desks.how_to_report: File at https://www.internet-signalement.gouv.fr/PharosWebReport/index.php — select 'scam/fraud' as the category, attach evidence; for urgent crypto-tracing victims also contact their local brigade or gendarmerie.

desks.name: Tracfin (Traitement du renseignement et action contre les circuits financiers clandestins)
desks.role: Financial intelligence unit (Ministry of Economy) that combats money laundering and clandestine financial circuits; receives reports/alerts on suspicious finance including crypto scams
desks.how_to_report: Individuals can report via the whistleblower channel https://www.economie.gouv.fr/tracfin/lanceur-dalerte-tracfin-recoit-vos-signalements ; professionals file suspicious-activity reports through the ERMES platform https://www.economie.gouv.fr/tracfin/ermes-la-plateforme-de-declaration-en-ligne-de-tracfin

desks.name: AMF Espace Épargnants (Autorité des marchés financiers)
desks.role: Securities regulator's investor-protection desk; maintains blacklists of unauthorized crypto/FX trading sites and takes victim reports
desks.how_to_report: Check/report unauthorized platforms at https://www.amf-france.org/fr/espace-epargnants/proteger-son-epargne/listes-noires-et-mises-en-garde ; the AMF Médiateur (https://www.amf-france.org/fr/le-mediateur) handles investor mediation.

steps: Freeze: Ask your bank for a 'rappel de virement' (transfer recall) immediately; notify your crypto exchange to freeze the withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Keep screenshots, emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and bank transfer receipts (RIB).
Report to exchange/bank: Notify the receiving platform so they can freeze and trace.
Report to police: File on Pharos (https://www.internet-signalement.gouv.fr/PharosWebReport/index.php) or at your local police/gendarmerie for a main courante.

Regulator: Report unauthorized investment platforms to AMF (https://www.amf-france.org/fr/espace-epargnants/proteger-son-epargne/listes-noires-et-mises-en-garde); report money-laundering leads to Tracfin (https://www.economie.gouv.fr/tracfin/lanceur-dalerte-tracfin-recoit-vos-signalements).

procedures.title: Spain: CNMV investor queries, Banco de España claims desk, Policía Nacional denuncia

desks.name: CNMV (Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores) — Investor queries/consultations
desks.role: Securities regulator; takes investor queries about unregistered trading platforms and maintains fraud warnings (chiringuitos financieros)
desks.how_to_report: Submit a query via https://www.cnmv.es/portal/inversor/Consultas.aspx; check authorized entities at https://www.cnmv.es/portal/inversor/Entidades-Autorizadas.aspx and consult their 'Decálogo - chiringuitos financieros' guidance.

desks.name: Banco de España — Servicio de Reclamaciones (claims service)
desks.role: Handles complaints/claims against banks and payment service providers, including unauthorized withdrawals
desks.how_to_report: File an electronic claim at https://sedeelectronica.bde.es/sede/es/tramites/reclamaciones-transparencia-buenas-practicas-p104.html after first exhausting the bank's own complaints procedure.

desks.name: Policía Nacional — Denuncias
desks.role: Police intake for criminal complaints (denuncias) of fraud and cybercrime
desks.how_to_report: File at the Policía Nacional denuncias desk https://www.policia.es/_es/denuncias.php, or at a local comisaría; for urgent crypto-tracing, banks can invoke SEPA recall procedures.

steps: Freeze: Immediately contact your bank to attempt a recall (Orden SEPA); notify the crypto exchange to freeze withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save all chats, emails, wallet addresses, txids, transfer receipts, and the scam site URL.
Report to exchange/bank: Notify the receiving platform for internal freeze/tracing.
Report to police: File a denuncia at Policía Nacional (https://www.policia.es/_es/denuncias.php) or Guardia Civil for rural areas.

Regulator: Query/report to CNMV (https://www.cnmv.es/portal/inversor/Consultas.aspx); file bank claims to Banco de España (https://sedeelectronica.bde.es/sede/es/tramites/reclamaciones-transparencia-buenas-practicas-p104.html).

procedures.title: Italy: Banca d'Italia banking/financial education desk, IVASS claims, Polizia di Stato

desks.name: Banca d'Italia — Tutela ed educazione (consumer protection & education)
desks.role: Central bank's consumer protection and financial-education desk; oversees banking complaints (ABF - Banking and Financial Ombudsman system)
desks.how_to_report: File a complaint with your bank first, then escalate via the ABF (Arbitro Bancario Finanziario) system listed on the Banca d'Italia tutela-educazione page https://www.bancaditalia.it/compiti/tutela-educazione/index.html

desks.name: IVASS (Istituto per la vigilanza sulle assicurazioni) — Reclami (insurance claims)
desks.role: Insurance regulator; handles complaints about insurance/investment products and fraud-related insurance issues
desks.how_to_report: File a reclamo (complaint) per the guidance at https://www.ivass.it/consumatori/reclami/index.html (guidance PDF and complaint form available there).

desks.name: Polizia di Stato / Comando Carabinieri
desks.role: Police intake for criminal complaints (querela/denuncia) for crypto scams, phishing, and unauthorized withdrawals
desks.how_to_report: File at the nearest commissariato or via the Polizia di Stato website; keep all wallet addresses and transfer receipts.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank for an urgent bonifico recall; ask your crypto exchange to freeze the withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save chats, emails, wallet addresses, txids, and bank receipts.
Report to exchange/bank: Notify the receiving platform so it can trace/freeze.
Report to police: File a querela/denuncia at the Polizia di Stato or Carabinieri.

Regulator/ombudsman: Escalate bank disputes via ABF (Banca d'Italia page https://www.bancaditalia.it/compiti/tutela-educazione/index.html); insurance/investment complaints to IVASS (https://www.ivass.it/consumatori/reclami/index.html).

procedures.title: Netherlands: Politie aangifte/melding, AFM consumer fraud desk

desks.name: Politie (Dutch National Police) — Aangifte of melding doen (filing reports)
desks.role: National police intake for criminal complaints (aangifte) or tips (melding) about fraud and crypto scams
desks.how_to_report: File online at https://www.politie.nl/aangifte-of-melding-doen (choose aangifte for criminal complaints, melding for tips); emergency: 112, non-urgent: 0900-8844.

desks.name: AFM (Autoriteit Financiële Markten) — Consumer fraud information
desks.role: Financial markets regulator; maintains warning lists of unauthorized investment firms and accepts consumer fraud reports
desks.how_to_report: See https://www.afm.nl/nl-nl/consumenten/waarschuwingen for guidance; report via AFM contact desk; check their unauthorized-firms warning list before investing.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank immediately for a SEPA recall; notify your crypto exchange to freeze the withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save chats, emails, wallet addresses, txids, and bank receipts.
Report to exchange: Notify the receiving platform so they can trace and freeze.
Report to police: File an aangifte at Politie (https://www.politie.nl/aangifte-of-melding-doen).
Regulator: Report to AFM (https://www.afm.nl/nl-nl/consumenten/waarschuwingen); also check DNB for payment-institution issues.

procedures.title: Canada: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC) and National Cybercrime Coordination Centre (NC3)

desks.name: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (Centre antifraude du Canada)
desks.role: National intake for fraud reports (investment scams, crypto fraud) run by RCMP/OPP; feeds national statistics and law-enforcement coordination
desks.how_to_report: File at https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/report-signalez-eng.htm or call 1-888-495-8501; gather bank/crypto details first.

desks.name: NC3 (National Cybercrime Coordination Centre) — Cyber.gc.ca incident reporting
desks.role: Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) cybercrime coordination; online reporting for cybercrime including crypto-related fraud
desks.how_to_report: Report cyber incidents at https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/incident-management ; local police can be engaged after CAFC files a report.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank immediately for a wire/Interac recall; notify your crypto exchange to freeze withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save chats, emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, transfer receipts, and the scam site URL.
Report to exchange: Notify the crypto exchange or bank for internal trace/freeze.
Report to police/CAFC: File with the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/report-signalez-eng.htm); your local police can use the CAFC report for investigation.
Regulator/cyber: Report cyber incident to NC3 via https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/incident-management ; for investment fraud also contact the provincial securities commission.

procedures.title: Australia: Scamwatch (ACCC) and ReportCyber (AFP/Australian Cyber Security Centre)

desks.name: Scamwatch (National Anti-Scam Centre, ACCC)
desks.role: National consumer-agency intake for scam reports (investment scams, crypto scams); feeds public warning data
desks.how_to_report: File at https://www.scamwatch.gov.au/report-a-scam ; include the amount, method of payment (crypto or bank), and scammer contact details.

desks.name: ReportCyber (Australian Federal Police / Australian Cyber Security Centre)
desks.role: National police/cyber-security online reporting system for cybercrime including cryptocurrency investment fraud
desks.how_to_report: File at https://www.cyber.gov.au/report-and-recover/report ; ReportCyber will route the report to the relevant state or federal law enforcement.

steps: Freeze: Contact your bank immediately (banks can attempt a recall); ask your crypto exchange to freeze withdrawal and comply with ASIC/AUSTRAC tracing.
Gather evidence: Keep chats, emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and bank transfer receipts.
Report to exchange: Notify the receiving exchange's fraud desk for internal freeze and trace.
Report to police: Use ReportCyber (https://www.cyber.gov.au/report-and-recover/report) and, if large amounts, contact your local police or AFP.
Regulator: Report to Scamwatch (https://www.scamwatch.gov.au/report-a-scam); for regulated investments also file with ASIC.

procedures.title: South Korea: Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원) and Korean National Police (경찰청) e-Complaint

desks.name: Financial Supervisory Service (금융감독원, FSS)
desks.role: Financial regulator; handles complaints about unauthorized withdrawals, illegal investment solicitation, and crypto-related fraud via its consumer complaint desk (1332 hotline)
desks.how_to_report: File via FSS online complaint system https://www.fss.or.kr/fss/bbs/B0000188/list.do or call 1332; the FSS can mediate with banks to freeze suspicious accounts.

desks.name: Korean National Police Agency (경찰청) — e-CRM e-Complaint (전자민원)
desks.role: Police intake for filing criminal complaints (고소/고발) of fraud and unauthorized withdrawals
desks.how_to_report: File at https://ecrm.police.go.kr/minwon/main or visit a local police station; for urgent transfers ask the bank to invoke the 'account freeze (계좌 동결)' for fraud under the 특정금융정보법.

steps: Freeze: Immediately call your bank to request a freeze on the transfer (계좌 동결) under Korea's fraud-victim relief regime; for crypto, notify the exchange (Upbit/Bithumb etc.) to freeze the withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save chats (KakaoTalk), emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and bank receipts.
Report to exchange/bank: Notify the receiving platform; banks coordinate with FSS and police for asset tracing.
Report to police: File at the Korean National Police e-Complaint portal (https://ecrm.police.go.kr/minwon/main) or a local station.
Regulator: File with FSS (https://www.fss.or.kr/fss/bbs/B0000188/list.do) for unauthorized withdrawals/illegal solicitation.

procedures.title: Singapore: ScamShield and Singapore Police Force (I-Witness / e-Services)

desks.name: ScamShield (NCPC / Ministry of Home Affairs)
desks.role: Government anti-scam platform; lets the public report scam calls, SMS/WhatsApp messages, and phishing sites; official scam-advisory database
desks.how_to_report: Report scam messages/numbers at https://scamshield.gov.sg/ ; install the ScamShield app for automatic blocking.

desks.name: Singapore Police Force — e-Services / i-Witness
desks.role: Police intake for police reports and information on fraud, including unauthorized withdrawals and crypto scams
desks.how_to_report: Submit a police report via https://www.police.gov.sg/e-services ; for emergency, call 999; for scam hotline, call 1800-722-6688.

steps: Freeze: Call your bank immediately (DBS/OCBC/UOB have 24h fraud hotlines) to attempt a freeze/recall; ask your crypto exchange to freeze the withdrawal.
Gather evidence: Save chats, emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and bank receipts.
Report to exchange/bank: Notify the receiving platform for internal tracing and cooperation with police.
Report to police: File a police report at https://www.police.gov.sg/e-services or at a Neighbourhood Police Post.
Report scams: Log the scam messages/numbers on ScamShield (https://scamshield.gov.sg/) so others can be protected.

procedures.title: International: INTERPOL financial crime, Chainabuse community reporting, IC3 crypto-recovery scam guidance

desks.name: INTERPOL — Financial Crime desk
desks.role: International criminal-police organization coordinating cross-border financial-crime investigations among member states
desks.how_to_report: INTERPOL does not take direct victim reports; victims should report to national police (who can request INTERPOL coordination) and use Chainabuse for blockchain-level reporting.

desks.name: Chainabuse (TRM Labs) — community crypto-scam reporting
desks.role: Cross-chain community platform to report scam wallet addresses, fake airdrops, and fraudulent DeFi sites; alerts other users and exchanges
desks.how_to_report: Submit a report at https://chainabuse.com/report with the wallet address, blockchain, txid, and evidence; reports are visible to partner exchanges for flagging.

desks.name: IC3 — cryptocurrency recovery scam guidance
desks.role: FBI IC3 publishes public service announcements warning victims about 'recovery' scams after crypto fraud and accepting new complaints
desks.how_to_report: Review IC3 PSAs at https://www.ic3.gov/PSA before engaging any self-described 'crypto recovery' service; file new/recovery-related complaints at https://complaint.ic3.gov/

steps: Freeze: Contact the crypto exchange hosting the scammer's wallet (if known) to request a freeze; in parallel contact your own bank/exchange for a recall.
Gather evidence: Preserve all chats/emails, wallet addresses, transaction hashes, and fiat-transfer receipts; use block explorers to document on-chain flows.
Report to exchange: Use Chainabuse (https://chainabuse.com/) to publicly flag the wallet, and notify the receiving exchange's compliance desk.
Report to police: File with your national police desk (see country entries); your report can be escalated internationally via INTERPOL by your national police, not directly by you.
Beware recovery scams: Do not pay any 'crypto recovery' service; check FBI IC3 guidance (https://www.ic3.gov/) and file a fresh IC3 complaint if you are targeted again.
